title: Digestive and Other Organ Systems
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Digestive and Other Organ Systems Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify major organs and organ systems (digestive, skeletal, muscular, nervous, excretory) and describe their functions and how they interact. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Human Organ Systems)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on digestion, organs, bones, muscles, nerves and the kidneys. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Organs work together in organ systems.
key_sub: The digestive system breaks down food; the skeleton supports; nerves carry messages.
body_html:
How to think about it

An organ system is a group of organs that work together to do a job.

  • Digestive system: mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine.
  • Skeletal and muscular systems hold you up and move you. Muscles pull on bones.
  • Nervous system: the brain, spinal cord and nerves carry messages.
  • Excretory system: the kidneys filter waste from the blood.
Example

Where are most nutrients absorbed?

after the stomach

a long tube with villi

Answer: the small intestine

Example

Which system protects the brain?

the skull is a bone

Answer: the skeletal system

Common mistakes

  • Thinking digestion happens only in the stomach.
  • Thinking muscles push bones (they only pull).
  • Mixing up the large and small intestine.

faq.q: What is the difference between an organ and an organ system?
faq.a: An organ is one body part with a job, like the stomach. An organ system is a group of organs working together, like the digestive system.

faq.q: How do organ systems work together?
faq.a: The digestive system gives nutrients, the circulatory system carries them, and the nervous system controls the body.

faq.q: Why is the small intestine so long?
faq.a: Its length and its tiny villi give a large surface to absorb nutrients into the blood.

items.q: Which organ system breaks food down so the body can use it?
items.e: Digestion breaks food into nutrients.

items.q: Food reaches the small intestine. Where has it just come from?
items.e: mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus.

items.q: Food leaves the small intestine. Where does it go next?
items.e: mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus.

items.q: Where does digestion begin?
items.e: Teeth chew food and saliva starts to digest it.

items.q: Does digestion take place in the large intestine?
c: Yes, it makes the most digestive juices.
No. Water is absorbed here, but food is not digested.
Yes, digested food is absorbed here.
items.e: Digestion takes place in the mouth, stomach and small intestine only.

items.q: Which of these parts does NOT produce digestive juices?
items.e: The esophagus only moves food to the stomach.

items.q: Why is the small intestine very long?
c: There is more time and surface for digested food to be absorbed.
items.e: A long small intestine absorbs more food.

items.q: Which organ does the brain work with to let you see?
items.e: Eyes send signals to the brain.

items.q: What do the teeth do in digestion?
c: They cut and grind food into smaller pieces.
items.e: Smaller pieces are easier to digest.

items.q: Which parts produce digestive juices?
c: the esophagus and the large intestine
the mouth, the stomach and the small intestine
items.e: Digestive juices break food down.

items.q: Why is food in the large intestine more solid than food in the small intestine?
c: Water has been absorbed from it.
items.e: The large intestine absorbs water.

items.q: Where are most nutrients absorbed into the blood?
items.e: The small intestine is long and lined with villi.

items.q: Why do we need a digestive system?
c: to break down food so the body can use it for energy and growth
to pump blood around the body
items.e: The body cannot use big pieces of food.

items.q: Does digestion take place in the small intestine?
c: No. Only water is absorbed here.
Yes. Food is broken down here with the help of digestive juices.
items.e: Digestion takes place in the mouth, stomach and small intestine.

items.q: What leaves the body through the anus?
items.e: Food that cannot be digested is removed.

items.q: Does digestion take place in the mouth?
c: No. Only water is absorbed here.
Yes. Food is broken down here with the help of digestive juices.
items.e: Digestion takes place in the mouth, stomach and small intestine.

items.q: Which part connects the mouth to the stomach?
items.e: The esophagus is a muscular tube.

items.q: Where is digested food absorbed into the blood?
items.e: The small intestine is long and has a large surface.

items.q: Does digestion take place in the stomach?
c: Yes. Food is broken down here with the help of digestive juices.
No. Only water is absorbed here.
items.e: Digestion takes place in the mouth, stomach and small intestine.

items.q: Which part of the digestive system is the longest?
items.e: The small intestine is about 6 m long in an adult.

items.q: What does the large intestine mainly do?
items.e: Water returns to the body.

items.q: Which statement about the esophagus is correct?
c: It moves food to the stomach by squeezing.
items.e: No digestion takes place in the esophagus.

items.q: In which two parts does NO digestion take place?
c: the stomach and the small intestine
the mouth and the small intestine
the esophagus and the large intestine
items.e: They do not produce digestive juices.

items.q: Arjun is studying the bones. Which organ system is this body part in?
items.e: The bones is part of the skeletal system, which supports the body and protects organs.

items.q: Noah is studying the diaphragm. Which organ system is this body part in?
items.e: The diaphragm is part of the respiratory system, which takes in oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.

items.q: Benjamin reads about a body system that collects information and sends messages that control the body. Which system is it?
items.e: The nervous system collects information and sends messages that control the body.

items.q: Chloe asks: what is the main job of the excretory system?
c: It moves blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell.
It supports the body and protects organs.
It removes wastes from the body.
It moves the body by pulling on bones.
items.e: The excretory system removes wastes from the body.

items.q: Maya is studying the blood. Which organ system is this body part in?
items.e: The blood is part of the circulatory system, which moves blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell.

items.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
c: tissue, cell, organ, organism, organ system
cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
organ, tissue, cell, organism, organ system
cell, organ, tissue, organ system, organism
items.e: Groups of cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems, and systems form the organism.

items.q: Ethan reads about a body system that breaks food down into nutrients the body can use. Which system is it?
items.e: The digestive system breaks food down into nutrients the body can use.

items.q: Which is the largest organ of the body?
items.e: Skin protects the body.

items.q: Ava is studying the skin (sweat). Which organ system is this body part in?
items.e: The skin (sweat) is part of the excretory system, which removes wastes from the body.

items.q: Which food group helps build strong bones?
items.e: Calcium builds bones.

items.q: A group of cells working together forms a(n) ____. What fills the blank?
items.e: Cells → tissue.

items.q: Liam is studying the spinal cord. Which organ system is this body part in?
items.e: The spinal cord is part of the nervous system, which collects information and sends messages that control the body.

items.q: Owen asks: what is the main job of the muscular system?
c: It takes in oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.
It supports the body and protects organs.
It moves blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell.
It moves the body by pulling on bones.
items.e: The muscular system moves the body by pulling on bones.

items.q: What do the kidneys do?
c: filter waste from the blood to make urine
items.e: The kidneys are part of the excretory system.

items.q: Which organ system sends messages between the brain and the body?
items.e: Nerves carry signals.

items.q: A group of tissues working together forms a(n) ____. What fills the blank?
items.e: Tissues → organ.

items.q: Noah is studying the nerves. Which organ system is this body part in?
items.e: The nerves is part of the nervous system, which collects information and sends messages that control the body.

items.q: Muscles work with which system to move the body?
items.e: Muscles pull on bones.

items.q: Lucas is studying the ribs. Which organ system is this body part in?
items.e: The ribs is part of the skeletal system, which supports the body and protects organs.

items.q: Noah asks: what is the main job of the skeletal system?
c: It supports the body and protects organs.
It moves blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell.
It moves the body by pulling on bones.
It collects information and sends messages that control the body.
items.e: The skeletal system supports the body and protects organs.

items.q: Muscles pull on arm bones to bend the elbow. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: Hana sees a car coming. Which sense organ takes in this information?
items.e: This information is taken in by the eyes (sight).

items.q: What happens to muscles that are exercised often?
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: Lucas tastes a bitter berry. Which sense organ takes in this information?
items.e: This information is taken in by the tongue (taste).

items.q: What does the jaw bone do?
c: It lets the arm lift and move.
It holds the bottom teeth and lets us chew.
It protects the spinal cord and holds the body upright.
items.e: Many bones protect soft organs.

items.q: Ethan hears the school bell. Which sense organ takes in this information?
items.e: This information is taken in by the ears (hearing).

items.q: Why do muscles work in pairs?
c: Muscles can only pull, so one pulls a bone one way and the other pulls it back.
Muscles are always both pulling at once.
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: Which organ is a muscle that never stops working?
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: Where in the body is the spine (backbone)?
items.e: Learn the main bones and where they are.

items.q: A helmet of bone covers the brain. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: The spine keeps us upright. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: Noah feels a sharp rock under his foot. Which sense organ takes in this information?
items.e: This information is taken in by the skin (touch).

items.q: Where in the body is the skull?
items.e: Learn the main bones and where they are.

items.q: When the biceps contracts, what does the triceps do?
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: What does the femur (thigh bone) do?
c: It protects the spinal cord and holds the body upright.
It is the longest bone and helps us stand and walk.
items.e: Many bones protect soft organs.

items.q: Which bone protect the heart and lungs?
items.e: Match the bone to its job.

items.q: When you straighten your arm, what does your triceps (back of the upper arm) do?
c: It contracts and pulls the lower arm straight.
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: What does a muscle do when it contracts?
c: It gets shorter and fatter and pulls on a bone.
It lets go of the bone.
It gets longer and pushes a bone.
items.e: Muscles pull bones by contracting. They work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

items.q: Ethan smells something burning in the oven. Which sense organ takes in this information?
items.e: This information is taken in by the nose (smell).

items.q: Finger bones and muscles let us write and grip. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: Fish: which nutrient is this food mainly a source of?
items.e: Fish are rich in protein.

items.q: In the same model, what does the food left inside the stocking represent?
c: undigested food that moves to the large intestine
items.e: Undigested food cannot pass into the blood.

items.q: What is the main job of fibre in our diet?
c: to keep every cell working and stop us getting dehydrated
to help food move through the gut
to keep us healthy and help the body work properly
items.e: Fibre: help food move through the gut.

items.q: A rabbit eats grass, clover and dandelion leaves. What kind of animal is it?
items.e: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.

items.q: Which nutrient's main job is to help the body grow and repair itself?
items.e: Protein: help the body grow and repair itself.

items.q: Olivia's grandfather has had part of his large intestine removed. Which problem is he most likely to have?
c: He cannot absorb as much water from undigested food.
He cannot digest food in his mouth.
items.e: The large intestine absorbs water.

items.q: Beans: which nutrient is this food mainly a source of?
items.e: Beans are rich in protein.

items.q: What is an organ?
c: a type of blood vessel only
a body part made of tissues that does a special job
items.e: The heart, lungs and stomach are organs.

items.q: A horse eats grass, hay and oats. What kind of animal is it?
items.e: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.

items.q: What is the main job of fat in our diet?
c: to keep every cell working and stop us getting dehydrated
to help food move through the gut
to store energy and keep us warm
to keep us healthy and help the body work properly
items.e: Fat: store energy and keep us warm.

items.q: Which nutrient's main job is to keep every cell working and stop us getting dehydrated?
items.e: Water: keep every cell working and stop us getting dehydrated.

items.q: A spider eats flies and other insects. What kind of animal is it?
items.e: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.

items.q: What is the main job of carbohydrates in our diet?
c: to keep us healthy and help the body work properly
to help the body grow and repair itself
to store energy and keep us warm
items.e: Carbohydrates: give us energy.

items.q: Ethan wants to find out if chewing longer makes bread taste sweeter. What should he change?
c: the time he chews the bread
items.e: Change one variable only.

items.q: Why do we need fibre in our food?
c: It helps food move through the intestines.
It helps us see in the dark.
items.e: Fibre is found in vegetables and whole grains.

items.q: A caterpillar eats leaves. What kind of animal is it?
items.e: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.

items.q: Carrots: which nutrient is this food mainly a source of?
items.e: Carrots are rich in vitamins and minerals.

items.q: Cream: which nutrient is this food mainly a source of?
items.e: Cream are rich in fat.

items.q: Potatoes: which nutrient is this food mainly a source of?
items.e: Potatoes are rich in carbohydrates.

items.q: Noodles: which nutrient is this food mainly a source of?
items.e: Noodles are rich in carbohydrates.
